QuestionStmt.S: If $\vec{a} = \hat{i} + \hat{j}$, $\vec{b} = 2\hat{i} - \hat{k}$ then the point of intersection of the lines $\vec{r} \times \vec{a} = \vec{b} \times \vec{a}$ and $\vec{r} \times \vec{b} = \vec{a} \times \vec{b}$ is

Solution.S:
Let $\vec{r} = x\hat{i} + y\hat{j} + z\hat{k}$.

From $\vec{r} \times \vec{a} = \vec{b} \times \vec{a}$:

$$(\vec{r} - \vec{b}) \times \vec{a} = 0$$

$$\begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ x-2 & y & z+1 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \end{vmatrix} = 0$$

$$(-z-1)\hat{i} - (-z-1)\hat{j} + (x-y-2)\hat{k} = 0$$

$$z = -1, \quad x - y = 2 \quad \text{(i)}$$

From $\vec{r} \times \vec{b} = \vec{a} \times \vec{b}$:

$$(\vec{r} - \vec{a}) \times \vec{b} = 0$$

$$\begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ x-1 & y-1 & z \\ 2 & 0 & -1 \end{vmatrix} = 0$$

$$(1-y)\hat{i} - (1-x-2z)\hat{j} + (2-2y)\hat{k} = 0$$

$$y = 1, \quad x + 2z = 1 \quad \text{(ii)}$$

Solving (i) and (ii): $x - 1 = 2 \Rightarrow x = 3$. Also $z = -1$.

Thus point is $(3, 1, -1)$, which corresponds to option B.
